summary: Accepted CodeWiki CLI-first distribution, CodeWiki prompt enforcement, and Pi Code foundation direction.

diff_table.current_state: System/API docs describe CodeWiki as a harness-independent API facade with Pi tools and adapters, but do not clearly name a CLI as the primary distribution surface for terminal-first use.
diff_table.current_project_state: System/API docs describe CodeWiki as a harness-independent API facade with Pi tools and adapters, but do not clearly name a CLI as the primary distribution surface for terminal-first use.
diff_table.desired_state: CodeWiki distribution is CLI-first for terminal use, with the core API kept as the stable semantic engine and Pi/other surfaces implemented as adapters over that API.
diff_table.agreed_change: Document CLI-first distribution in product/system truth; preserve API facade as canonical engine; treat Pi extension as adapter rather than product core.
diff_table.expected_final_state: Product/system docs state that CodeWiki ships as a CLI plus optional adapters, all powered by the same core API; roadmap/planning can later create implementation work for CLI hardening if needed.
diff_table.rationale: Terminal-first use needs a first-class distribution surface, but duplicating semantics outside the API would fragment behavior across CLI, Pi, daemon, and future integrations.
diff_table.risk: medium semantic-system direction; docs-only in this task, possible future source work for CLI packaging.
alternatives: Make Pi extension the primary distribution and keep CLI secondary.
Expose only library/API without a CLI.
Build a separate CLI implementation that bypasses the API.

diff_table.current_state: Main skill name is `codewiki`; workflow skill names are `codewiki-*`; public tool names use `wiki_*`.
diff_table.current_project_state: Main skill name is `codewiki`; workflow skill names are `codewiki-*`; public tool names use `wiki_*`.
diff_table.desired_state: Keep the main router skill named `codewiki` because it is a specific product/router name and avoids a generic `wiki` collision; keep or migrate workflow skills only through a staged compatibility plan.
diff_table.agreed_change: Prefer `codewiki` for the main skill/router. Treat skill names as agent-internal progressive-disclosure assets, not the primary public API. If workflow skill names change, do it as a compatibility-backed migration.
diff_table.expected_final_state: Agents see one clear CodeWiki router skill, public users see `codewiki` CLI and `wiki_*` tools, and no duplicate generic `wiki` skill confuses skill selection.
diff_table.rationale: Agent skill discovery benefits from unique, product-specific names; `wiki` is too generic and can collide. Tool/CLI consistency matters, but hard skill renames can break installed references.
alternatives: Rename main skill to `wiki`.
Duplicate both `wiki` and `codewiki` main skills.
Keep every skill name unchanged forever.

diff_table.current_state: CodeWiki behavior is primarily enforced by on-demand skills, tools, project AGENTS.md, and user discipline; models can ignore skill loading or forget CodeWiki invariants.
diff_table.current_project_state: CodeWiki behavior is primarily enforced by on-demand skills, tools, project AGENTS.md, and user discipline; models can ignore skill loading or forget CodeWiki invariants.
diff_table.desired_state: CodeWiki extension injects a small always-on system-prompt contract when a repo has CodeWiki installed/configured, while detailed loop instructions remain in on-demand skills.
diff_table.agreed_change: Add a bounded CodeWiki system-prompt contract via Pi extension hooks for installed CodeWiki projects: use `wiki_state`, respect canonical/generated/runtime boundaries, route semantic changes through decision/planning/implementation/validation, and avoid hand-editing generated state.
diff_table.expected_final_state: Agents in CodeWiki repos get hard prompt-level invariants before each turn, with skills remaining progressive detail; non-CodeWiki projects are unaffected.
diff_table.rationale: System prompt injection is stronger and more reliable than skills alone, but full skill content in the system prompt would bloat context and overfit every turn.
alternatives: Move the full CodeWiki skill into every Pi base system prompt.
Use only skills and no prompt injection.
Inject prompt globally even outside CodeWiki repos.

diff_table.current_state: CodeWiki is currently a Pi package/extension during development, while Pi Code is the generic foundation harness.
diff_table.current_project_state: CodeWiki is currently a Pi package/extension during development, while Pi Code is the generic foundation harness.
diff_table.desired_state: Long-term distribution is `codewiki` as an opinionated terminal coding system built on Pi Code foundation: users install/run CodeWiki for CodeWiki workflow, while Pi Code remains the engine/foundation dependency.
diff_table.agreed_change: Position CodeWiki as CLI-first and CodeWiki-owned prompt/API/tool policy over Pi Code foundation, not as a fork of Pi internals. During development it remains a Pi extension; later it can expose a `codewiki` entrypoint that loads Pi Code with CodeWiki defaults.
diff_table.expected_final_state: `codewiki` command starts the CodeWiki-enabled experience; core API remains semantic engine; Pi extension remains development/compatibility path; Pi Code stays minimal foundation.
diff_table.rationale: This gives CodeWiki stronger workflow enforcement and user-facing distribution without weakening Pi's generic extension model or duplicating engine internals.
alternatives: Keep CodeWiki only as an optional Pi extension forever.
Fork Pi Code and hard-code CodeWiki into it.
Make CodeWiki a library/API only with no terminal distribution.

diff_table.current_state: CodeWiki tool names use the `wiki_*` convention, while skill names and folders use `codewiki`, `codewiki-decision`, `codewiki-planning`, `codewiki-implementation`, and `codewiki-validation`.
diff_table.current_project_state: CodeWiki tool names use the `wiki_*` convention, while skill names and folders use `codewiki`, `codewiki-decision`, `codewiki-planning`, `codewiki-implementation`, and `codewiki-validation`.
diff_table.desired_state: Public/user-facing skill names align with the `wiki_*` workflow naming convention, e.g. `wiki-decision`/`wiki_decision`, while old `codewiki-*` names remain as compatibility aliases or migration refs during transition.
diff_table.agreed_change: Deferred. Latest accepted direction keeps main skill `codewiki` and treats workflow skill renames as non-urgent compatibility-backed migration work, not current implementation scope.
diff_table.expected_final_state: No current hard rename. Future planning may revisit skill aliases after CLI and prompt-contract work are scoped.
diff_table.rationale: Consistent names reduce user confusion, but prompt-contract enforcement and CLI/API clarity matter more than skill folder renames; hard renames can break references.
alternatives: Keep codewiki-* skill names as internal implementation labels.
Rename folders immediately without compatibility aliases.
Only document that skills are internal and tools are the public surface.

accepted_decisions.summary: CodeWiki CLI is the long-term terminal-first distribution surface.
Core API remains the semantic engine used by CLI, Pi, MCP, and future adapters.
Pi Code remains CodeWiki's foundation runtime; do not fork unless a concrete hook/SDK blocker appears.
CodeWiki extension should inject a small repo-scoped system-prompt contract rather than moving full skills into Pi's base prompt.
Main router skill remains named `codewiki`; workflow skill renaming is deferred.
